advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm pycontribs `search_issues(fields=None)` returns the same field set as omitting `fields` (esp. `issuelinks`); if not, have `_paged_search` omit `fields` when it is None, or pass an explicit field list per caller.
evidence: transport.py:406-407 (old path, public method): `lambda: self._client.search_issues(jql, startAt=start_at, maxResults=max_results)` — no `fields=` argument, library default applies

transport.py:443-445 (new path): `self._client.search_issues(jql, startAt=offset, maxResults=page_size, fields=fields)` with `_paged_search(..., fields: str | None = None, ...)` so `get_issuelinks_map`/`get_comment_map` now send `fields=None` explicitly
ABSENCE: the `jira` extra is not installed (resolve_symbol UNRESOLVED for `jira.JIRA.search_issues`), so the library's handling of `fields=None` vs the string default cannot be confirmed here

ABSENCE: `_PageCappingClient.search_issues(self, jql, startAt=0, maxResults=50, fields=None, **kw)` ignores `fields` (test file line 51-52), so no test would catch a payload regression caused by `fields=None`
advisory.finding: `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map` now flow through `_paged_search`, which always passes `fields=fields` to the library `search_issues` — defaulting to `fields=None`. The previous code called the public `self.search_issues(jql)` which passed NO `fields` kwarg, letting the pycontribs default (`"*all"`) apply. Explicitly forcing `fields=None` can change which fields the REST response carries and may omit `issuelinks`, silently defeating the paging fix.
advisory.suggested_fix: When `fields is None`, do not pass `fields=` to the library call (build kwargs conditionally), or pass an explicit field list (`"issuelinks"` for the links map) so the returned payload is guaranteed to include the needed fields.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the AST guard tolerate a page size supplied positionally (or document that the transport must always pass the cap by keyword).
evidence: test file lines 159-162: `kwargs = {kw.arg for kw in node.keywords}` then `if not ({"maxResults", "max_results"} & kwargs): offenders.append(...)` — only keyword args are inspected, positional args are ignored
transport.py:403-404: public `search_issues(self, jql, start_at=0, max_results=50)` accepts the cap positionally, so a positional call site is a legitimate, capped usage the guard would flag
advisory.finding: The structural AST guard only accepts a `maxResults`/`max_results` passed as a KEYWORD argument; a correctly page-sized but positional call (e.g. `self.search_issues(jql, 0, 100)`, valid against the public signature) would be reported as an offender and fail the build.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert (via caplog) that get_parent_map emits a WARNING on the exploding-client path, not only that it returns {}, so the 'WARNING + {}' degradation contract is fully pinned.
evidence: `assert _transport(_ExplodingClient()).get_parent_map("DC") == {}` (line 125) — the only assertion; no caplog / warning check anywhere in the module (search for `caplog`/`warning` returned no matches)
Docstring line 117-119: "promises the inbound pass a SOFT failure: log a WARNING and return {}" — the WARNING half is stated but not asserted

transport.py:576-582 — the degradation path both `logger.warning(...)` and `return {}`; and an empty project (transport.py:448 `if not batch: break`) also returns {}, so `== {}` does not distinguish 'degraded, logged' from 'silently returned {} without logging'
Ticket 9263 acceptance criterion: "its degradation contract (WARNING + {}) both still pass"
_call_logged docstring (transport.py:279): this log 'is the only signal those paths emit' — dropping it is exactly the silent-convergence failure the ticket exists to prevent
advisory.finding: test_get_parent_map_degradation_contract_is_preserved pins only the `{}` return of get_parent_map's degradation contract and never asserts the WARNING is logged, though the test's own docstring and the ticket both frame the contract as 'WARNING + {}'. An empty project also returns {}, so a regression that dropped the log (returning {} silently) would still pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `caplog` fixture and assert `logging.WARNING` records with 'get_parent_map degraded' text are present (and, for contrast, absent on the empty-project path), alongside the existing `== {}` assertion.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict `get_issuelinks_map`/`get_comment_map` to the fields they use (e.g. `_paged_search(..., fields="issuelinks")` / `fields="key"`) instead of fetching all default fields for the whole project.
evidence: transport.py:455 `issues = self._paged_search(f"project = {project_key}")` — no `fields=` argument, so `_paged_search` defaults `fields=None`

transport.py:469 `get_comment_map` also calls `self._paged_search(f"project = {project_key}")` with no `fields=`, and its loop (471-474) uses only `issue["key"]`, fetching comments via a separate call
Contrast: `get_parent_map` correctly restricts to `self._paged_search(query, fields="parent")` at transport.py:567

Because `_paged_search` (transport.py:437-452) pages to exhaustion, the full-field payload is now fetched for the entire project rather than a single 50-issue page — over-fetch amplified by project size
advisory.finding: `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map` fetch every default field for every issue across the whole project (`_paged_search(...)` passes no `fields=`, so `fields=None` reaches `search_issues`), yet use only `key`+`issuelinks` (or only `key`). Now that the change pages to exhaustion, this over-fetch scales with project size instead of being capped at ~50 issues.
scenarios: A large DC project (thousands of issues) where each issue carries a heavy default-field payload; the whole set is materialized to build a link/comment map that reads one field.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pass `fields="issuelinks"` from `get_issuelinks_map` and a minimal field set (e.g. `fields="key"`) from `get_comment_map`, mirroring `get_parent_map`'s `fields="parent"`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Batch comment retrieval in `get_comment_map` (e.g. expand comments in the paged search or fetch in batches) rather than one `comments()` round-trip per issue across the whole project.
evidence: transport.py:471-474 `for issue in issues: ... comments = _with_connection_retry(lambda k=key: self._client.comments(k))` — one remote call per issue

transport.py:469 the driving `issues` now comes from `self._paged_search(...)`, which pages to exhaustion (transport.py:437-452), so the loop iterates over the entire project rather than a single 50-issue page
Test `test_get_comment_map_pages_to_exhaustion_and_fetches_each_issue` asserts `len(client.comment_calls) == 250`, confirming one call per issue at full project scale
advisory.finding: `get_comment_map` issues one remote `comments()` call per issue (N+1). This loop is unchanged by the diff, but the pagination fix removes the former implicit 50-issue cap, so the number of per-issue round-trips is now unbounded by project size.
scenarios: A project with thousands of issues: `get_comment_map` now issues one `comments()` round-trip per issue across the entire project, where it previously issued at most 50.
